chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said:
The boundary of Al-Aqeeq is what is between Al-Maslakh up to Aqaba Ghamra.

key_terms.الْعَقِيقِ: Al-Aqeeq, a valley and place near Mecca used as a miqat (boundary) for Ihram
key_terms.الْمَسْلَخِ: Al-Maslakh, a specific location marking the start of the boundary
key_terms.عَقَبَةِ غَمْرَةَ: Aqabat Ghamra, a pass or location marking the end of the boundary

ai.seo_question: What is the defined boundary of Al-Aqeeq for entering the state of Ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the precise geographical limits of Al-Aqeeq, serving as a critical miqat (boundary) for pilgrims entering the state of Ihram for Hajj. By specifying the span from Al-Maslakh to Aqabat Ghamra, it provides the jurisprudential clarity necessary for the validity of ritual consecration, reflecting the Shia emphasis on adhering to established sacred boundaries.

en.hubeali:
A number of our ompanions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said: ‘
The boundary of Al-Aqeeq is what is between Al-Maslakh up to Aqaba Ghamra’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn abu Hamzah from abu Basir who has said the following: “One of the two Imam, (abu Ja’far or abu ‘Abd Allah), ‘Alayhim al-Salam, has said,
The limits of al-‘Aqiq is from al-Maslakh to ‘Aqabah.’”
